jobs.title: R&D Technical Coordinator - Career - Request #37590824
jobs.description: Job Title: R&D Technical Coordinator - CareerPosition Overview:Join our team and play a key role in the testing and production of integrated circuits (ICs) at the wafer stage. This position supports both production and prototype circuits within a high-variety manufacturing environment focused on advanced RF/microwave technologies.Located in Santa Rosa, California, this role offers the opportunity to work with sophisticated automated test systems while developing your technical expertise in electronics, RF testing, manufacturing, and troubleshooting.You will perform DC and RF testing, operate and maintain manufacturing equipment, troubleshoot technical issues, and work closely with engineers and other technical teams to resolve product and process challenges.Key Responsibilities:Perform DC and RF testing of integrated circuits using automated test systems and specialized test equipment.Set up, operate, maintain, and troubleshoot manufacturing and test equipment.Conduct product tests, experiments, measurements, and technical evaluations.Troubleshoot issues involving components, parts, products, equipment, and manufacturing processes.Provide technical support for electronic and mechanical operations.Assist engineers with product and process investigations and problem resolution.Analyze test results and use sound technical judgment to identify and resolve issues.Handle and test integrated circuit wafers in a controlled cleanroom environment.Follow established manufacturing, testing, safety, and quality procedures.Maintain accurate test and production records.Work effectively in a high-variety manufacturing environment with changing priorities.Collaborate across engineering, manufacturing, and other technical departments.Required & Preferred QualificationsAssociate degree (AS) or certificate in Electronics Technology preferred.Manufacturing experience preferred.Technical experience in electronics testing, troubleshooting, or related areas preferred.Experience working with integrated circuit wafers, including fabrication processes or wafer handling, preferred.Experience using a microscope.Ability to work in a cleanroom environment, including wearing required gowning and hood.Strong PC and Microsoft Office skills.Strong organizational and logistical skills.Excellent written and verbal communication skills.Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary, cross-functional environment.Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.Demonstrated interest in rapid skill development and progressively increasing responsibility.Experience with electronic test equipment preferred, including:Network analyzersSignal generatorsOscilloscopesSpectrum analyzersPower suppliesPower metersPay Transparency:This is the pay range that Magnit reasonably expects to pay someone for this position is $23.99/hour - $31.99/hour W-2.Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K (provided minimum eligibility hours are met).What You'll Bring:The ideal candidate is technically curious, detail-oriented, and comfortable working with electronic equipment in a manufacturing environment. You should be able to follow established procedures while also applying sound judgment when troubleshooting unexpected technical issues.This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to expand their expertise in RF/microwave testing, integrated circuit manufacturing, automated test systems, and electronics troubleshooting while working alongside experienced engineers and technical professionals.

jobs.title: Risk Analytics & Financial Systems Analyst
jobs.description: Title: Risk Analytics & Financial Systems AnalystLocation: 550 S 4th St, Minneapolis, MNDuration: 6 monthsWork Engagement: W2Work Schedule: 3 days in office/2 days remoteBenefits on offer for this contract position: Health Insurance, Life insurance, 401K and Voluntary BenefitsSummary:This contractor will support internal business partners who rely on risk and investment reporting. The primary focus of the role is assisting with report upgrades, validating system changes, and performing regression testing to ensure reports, calculations, and data feeds continue to function as expected.This is a finance-focused analytics role requiring an understanding of investment accounting, securities, and financial systems. (preferred)

to analyze prospective customer needs and match to appropriate company products and services.Conduct plan comparison and analysis for new or existing members seeking new solutions.Present and explain recommended products, benefits, features, and alternatives.Ensure new customers receive orientations/information regarding self-service and shopping tools, incentives and value-added features and information.Promote the additional services available to members through the center clinicians and service consultants.Cross-sell multiple product sets to deliver additional value to members and the management tactics to previous or prospective customers to drive sales.Perform outbound call campaigns to company generated sales leads.Perform outbound call campaigns for the Under 65 and Over 65 segmentGenerate referrals from existing client base through proactive outreach, relationship building, and delivering a best-in-class experience.Identify and contact at-risk customers; develop and execute retention strategies with solutions that meet customer needs.Set appointments for sales and member retention visits through various campaigns.Maintain an ongoing relationship with previous customers to drive retention and loyalty.Follow standard operating procedures to effectively disposition, track, and record outcomes of work efforts.Help facilitate enrollment or education meetings with prospective or existing customers within the retail center and within community settings.Gain personal understanding of targeted groups’ products, services and features.Conduct formal and enrollment support activities and outcomes.Community engagement + business development:Develop and execute a personal business development plan inclusive of internal and external community engagement tactics to support individual and team goal attainment throughout the year.Perform local grassroots marketing, networking, event activation, and relationship building outside of the center to drive growth and advance the company mission.Build and foster relationships with key constituents, organizations, networking groups, etc. to build community awareness of the center services.Travel to GEDLicenses/Certification DetailsState of Florida 2-15/2-40 licenseCurrent Federally Facilitated Marketplace (FFM) certificationAdditional Required Qualifications:Excellent verbal and written communication skills.Proficient with MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Internet and web-based tools.Work flexible hours to include evenings, weekends and holidays.Demonstrated ability to meet/exceed sales jobs.description: Overview:Provide Level 2/3 application support to KPMG clients and users of Oracle Cloud Applications and/or Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS). This role supports day-to-day operations, drives continuous improvement initiatives, manages production support activities, and ensures stability across Oracle enterprise platforms supporting Finance, Supply Chain, Procurement, Order Management, and Revenue Management processes. Responsibilities:- Application Support & Maintenance • Oversee day-to-day maintenance activities across Oracle applications and integrated enterprise platforms. • Manage issue diagnosis, break/fix activities, incident resolution, problem management, and root-cause analysis for order management, procurement, inventory, billing, invoicing, revenue recognition, and financial processes. • Lead a team responsible for configuration updates, testing, regression cycles, release management, and deployment support. • Monitor application health, interface processing, scheduled jobs, and integrations to ensure operational stability and SLA compliance. • Coordinate support activities across Oracle Cloud quarterly releases and platform upgrades. - Business Process & Requirement Management • Identify, document, and manage client business and functional requirements. • Assess client needs and assist in developing functional specifications for enhancements, configurations, and process improvements. • Drive operational efficiency through business process optimization and automation across Finance, Supply Chain, Procurement, Revenue Management, and Customer-to-Cash processes. • Collaborate with business stakeholders to evaluate enhancement requests and prioritize production support activities. - Delivery & Collaboration • Collaborate closely with onshore and offshore delivery teams using Agile and ITIL-based support frameworks. • Assist in reviewing functional specifications, test scripts, user stories, and operational documentation. • Partner with technical teams to support integrations between Oracle applications and third-party platforms including CRM, payment gateways, tax engines, banking systems, middleware, and data warehouses. • Support release planning, deployment validation, and post-production stabilization activities. - Build API-led integration architectures connecting SAP S/4HANA with other applications •Define event-driven and service-oriented integration patterns. • Establish API governance, monitoring, and security standards. jobs.title: SAP S/4HANA Finance Solution Architect
jobs.description: SAP S/4HANA Finance Solution Architect We are seeking an experienced SAP S/4HANA Finance Solution Architect to lead the design, architecture, and configuration of SAP S/4HANA Finance solutions. This role will be responsible for defining finance transformation strategies, driving adoption of SAP leading practices, and ensuring scalable, compliant, and maintainable solutions across global finance organizations. The ideal candidate will possess deep expertise in SAP S/4HANA Finance, including Financial Accounting (FI), Controlling (CO), Asset Accounting, Project Accounting, Revenue Recognition, Record-to-Report (RTR), and financial reporting. The architect will serve as the primary advisor for finance process design, configuration decisions, solution governance, and business transformation initiatives. Relevant SAP S/4 leading practices include standardized end-to-end finance processes, embedded analytics, integrated finance and controlling, and adoption of SAP Fiori user experiences. Responsibilities:Solution Architect and Design• Lead the end-to-end architecture and solution design for SAP S/4HANA Finance transformations. • Define future-state finance operating models leveraging SAP best practices and standard functionality. • Design scalable and maintainable solutions aligned with SAP Clean Core principles. • Provide thought leadership on finance process transformation and ERP modernization initiatives. • Evaluate business requirements and recommend optimal SAP standard capabilities before customizations. Finance Process Leadership • Serve as the functional architecture lead across key finance domains: General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Asset Accounting, Cost Center Accounting, Profit Center Accounting, Internal Orders, Project Accounting, Revenue Recognition, Consolidation and Financial Reporting, Treasury and Cash Management • Lead finance process redesign workshops and drive adoption of SAP leading practices. • Partner with Finance leadership to align business requirements with SAP solution capabilities. SAP Configuration Leadership • Lead and govern SAP S/4HANA Finance configuration activities. • Define configuration standards for: Ledger Design, Company Codes, Chart of Accounts, Fiscal Year Variants, Posting Period Controls, Financial Statement Versions, Costing Structures, Parallel Accounting, Universal Journal (ACDOCA) • Review and approve functional specifications, configuration documents, and solution designs. • Ensure consistency across global deployments and member firm implementations. Ledger and accounting-principle design are critical tenant-level architecture decisions that affect reporting, compliance, and operational processes. Reporting, Analytics & Controls • Architect financial reporting solutions utilizing: SAP Embedded Analytics, SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), Financial Reporting Structures • Design solutions that support regulatory, statutory, management, and operational reporting requirements. • Ensure strong internal controls and auditability across financial processes. • Support finance organizations with KPI frameworks and executive reporting capabilities. Embedded analytics and integrated FI/CO reporting are key SAP S/4HANA finance leading practices. Stakeholder Leadership • Facilitate executive and business stakeholder workshops.• Serve as trusted advisor to CFO organizations and finance leadership teams.• Collaborate closely with Enterprise Architects, Data Migration Teams, Integration Teams, Reporting, Teams, Security Teams, SAP Delivery Partners.• Present recommendations and architecture decisions to leadership governance boards. Delivery Leadership • Provide solution governance across all project phases: Discover, Design, Build, Test, Deploy, Hypercare • Support testing strategy, defect resolution, cutover planning, and production readiness activities. • Mentor SAP FI/CO consultants, business analysts, and functional leads. Qualifications:• Minimum ten years of recent SAP Finance consulting experience. • Minimum five years serving as SAP Finance Lead or Solution Architect. • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, information systems, computer science, or related discipline from an accredited college or university • Multiple end-to-end SAP S/4HANA implementation programs. • Extensive experience leading global finance transformation initiatives. • Experience working directly with CFO organizations and Finance leadership. • Deep expertise in: SAP S/4HANA Finance, Financial Accounting (FI), Controlling (CO), Universal Journal (ACDOCA), Asset Accounting, Project Systems / Professional Services, Revenue Recognition, Margin Analysis (CO-PA), Group Reporting, Financial Close Processes, Embedded Analytics, SAP Fiori • Knowledge of SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud configuration and core organizational and financial design concepts is highly desirable.• Strong understanding of: Record-to-Report (RTR), Procure-to-Pay (P2P), Order-to-Cash (O2C), Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Project Financials, Revenue and Billing Processes, Internal Controls and Compliance, Professional Services Finance Operations.• Possess business expertise, solid leadership skills, strong executive communication skills with the ability to influence senior stakeholders. • Resource should be located within commuting distance of Montvale, Dallas, or Chicago. jobs.title: NDT Quality Test Spec 3
jobs.description: This posting is for a contract assignment and is not a full-time employment offer with Boeing. Candidates selected for roles will be employed as contract workers through a Boeing approved 3rd party for the duration of the specified project.Responsible for performing and overseeing nondestructive testing (NDT) procedures in accordance with NAS410/BSS7698 standards. This role is critical in ensuring the integrity and safety of aerospace components and systems. The technician will utilize various NDT methods, including but not limited to ultrasonic, eddy current, radiographic, magnetic particle, and dye penetrant testing, to detect defects and ensure compliance with industry standards.Key Responsibilities:• Have the skills and knowledge to set up and standardize equipment, conduct system performance checks, process parts, interpret and evaluate for acceptance or rejection, and document results.• Successfully obtain the formal training hours required for any method where certification is being pursued, and any additional add-on formal training required by the company based on the demands of the business. (e.g. Computed Tomography training).• Be thoroughly familiar with the scope and limitations of the technique and/or method in which they are certified.• Assist in the development and implementation of NDT procedures and work instructions.• Have the skills and knowledge to conduct system performance checks in accordance with the applicable process standard.• Be familiar with the codes, standards, and other contractual specifications that control the Method used at their Site.• Be capable of providing the necessary guidance and/or supervision to trainees and Level 1 personnel in the technique and/or method in which they are certified and applicable safety protocols.• Have a basic knowledge of relevant product manufacturing and inspection technology.• Maintain NDT equipment and ensure it is calibrated and functioning correctly.• Inspect and report any issues with or damage to reference standards used to perform the approved technique to the method level 3 and NDT manager.• Collaborate with engineering and quality assurance teams to address any non-conformance issues.• Participate in audits and inspections as required by regulatory bodies and internal quality systems.• Stay current with industry standards, advancements in NDT technology, and best practices.• Have basic knowledge of aircraft or vehicle maintenance.• Be capable of developing written work instructions from approved general procedures. Such instructions require final approval by an Engineer Level 3, or Level 3 certified in the method.• May be delegated to perform certain method surveillances in EPES, and also work to address any findings identified in an EPES surveillance when required.Qualifications:• Education: High school diploma or equivalent; technical degree in a related field preferred. Documented formal training in Nondestructive testing is required but may be added as necessary.• Certification: NAS410/BSS7698 Level 2 certification in at least one NDT method (e.g., Ultrasonic).• Skills: o Strong understanding of NDT principles and techniques.o Proficient in reading and interpreting engineering drawings and specifications.o Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills.o Strong ethical standards with a desire to maintain a high level of quality.o Strong communication skills, both verbal and written.o Ability to work independently and as part of a team.Location/Training Comments:Candidates must be willing to train outside of the Washington location listed to obtain the NDT certification.

jobs.description: Job Description: Support end-to-end campaign audience build, measurement, and reporting for prioritized Growth Marketing campaigns — translating marketing objectives into audience specifications, measurement requirements, and dashboards that campaign owners can act on.Core ResponsibilitiesCampaign audience builds — translate eligibility and targeting criteria into audience specs, size audiences, validate against holdout and targeting logic, and re-validate after platform changes.Measurement & reporting requirements — define campaign signals, KPIs, and reporting specifications per campaign; feasibility-check proposed solutions with stakeholders before build.Dashboards & QA — build and maintain campaign dashboard suites (operational visibility plus quarterly performance reporting), monitoring and alerting, and automated QA frameworks; update pipelines when data sources change.Campaign triage — identify measurement and reporting gaps, drive resolution with MarTech and Data Engineering, and document outcomes.Insights & readouts — ad hoc analyses, performance deep-dives, and quarterly reporting packages.Documentation — keep runbooks, troubleshooting guides, and the team knowledge repository current.Automation & AI-assisted workflows — identify repeat manual steps in campaign build and reporting and automate them, including AI/agent-based analytical workflows where appropriate.Must have:experience in analytics or data science — marketing analytics, growth/campaign analytics, CRM analytics, product analytics, or a quantitative data science role.Degree or equivalent practical background in a quantitative field (statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science, engineering, or similar).Advanced SQL — able to write performant queries against large, messy datasets and build reproducible, well-documented logic.Python (or R) for analysis and automation: data wrangling, scripting, and repeatable reporting.Applied statistics — experiment design, A/B testing, significance and power, incrementality and holdout measurement, and the judgment to know when a result is not real.Hands-on dashboarding and data modeling; comfortable owning a pipeline or dashboard end-to-end, not only consuming one.Demonstrated ability to take an ambiguous marketing question, scope it into an analytical plan, and deliver a recommendation non-technical stakeholders can act on.Works autonomously across multiple concurrent campaign timelines with limited direction.Nice to day:AI/ML experience — practical use of LLMs or agentic tooling to accelerate analysis, reporting, or QA (prompt design, agent workflows, evaluating output quality), and/or applied ML such as propensity and lifetime-value modeling, segmentation, uplift modeling, or forecasting.Causal inference beyond basic A/B testing — difference-in-differences, geo experiments, synthetic control, matching.Marketing automation / martech platform exposure — Salesforce-type marketing clouds, email and messaging channels, audience management tools.Lifecycle or CRM marketing measurement at scale; This role focuses on render-path DSP tuning of the speaker system using Meta's internally-developed embedded audio processing framework and tuning tools. Perform speaker render-path tuning for research AR glasses using the company's internally-developed embedded audio DSP framework and associated MATLAB-based tuning toolsTuning Components: Design and speaker integritySpeaker Characterization & Baseline Measurement: Measure devices to establish baseline performance, collect frequency response, distortion (THD), and impedance data in anechoic or controlled acoustic environmentsTuning Profile Management: Generate, compile, and validate tuning profiles via Meta's internal tuning toolchain for deployment to device firmwareCollaboration with Cross-Functional Teams: Work with hardware, firmware, algorithms, and research teams to align tuning with system-level requirementsDocumentation: Maintain tuning documentation, test reports, and configuration records for each tuning iteration and release candidateTool Onboarding: Ramp up on Meta's internal audio DSP ecosystem including graphical pipeline editors, render tuning tools, and device control utilities with support from internal tooling teamsRequired QualificationsPrior experience performing audio systems render tuning for consumer electronics products (AR/VR glasses, hearables, headphones, wearables, telecom devices, smart speakers)Understanding of render DSP tuning approaches (EQ, DRC, limiting, speaker protection) and hands-on experience performing tuning in a lab environmentExperience with electroacoustic measurement tools (e.g. Audio Precision (APx series), Listen SoundCheck, HEAD acoustics ACQUA) and measurement transducersExperience with MATLAB for audio signal processing, filter design, and tuning tool workflowsStrong attention to detail and systematic approach to parameter optimization and documentationAbility to work independently on tuning tasks while collaborating with a broader audio engineering teamUnderstanding of speaker protection algorithms (excursion limiting, thermal protection, brownout protection)Bachelor's degree in characterization (T/S parameters, Klippel, impedance, excursion)Exposure to DSP frameworks or audio middleware (AudioWeaver, Qualcomm QACT, or similar embedded audio toolchains)Experience with volume table tuning and perceptual loudness optimizationExposure to firmware-level audio bring-up or ADSP integration workflowsExperience with capture-path audio tuning including any of beamforming and The successful candidate will be responsible for developing and monitoring quality program metrics, analyzing trends, and working with applicable parties to correct any issues. This role will also involve assisting with the development of on-site partner construction QA and QC teams, as well as providing training to personnel regarding awareness and quality procedures. Interface between design, construction, and facility operations as well as general contractor(s). Provide training to personnel regarding awareness and quality procedures and specific responsibilities in the QA/QC process. jobs.description: Summary:We're looking for a seasoned CW Product Marketing Manager to drive successful market entry and accelerate growth across global markets for our wearables portfolio. They are an organized self-starter who proactively identifies and solves problems, and they thrive in a fast-paced, cross-functional, action-oriented environment.A successful candidate will bring a combination of strategic vision, data-driven decision-making, exceptional cross-functional leadership, and hands-on product launch experience.ResponsibilitiesGo-to-Market Execution: Own and operationalize clear GTM strategies for new market launches, bringing a strong point of view to strategic decisions and tradeoffs (product readiness, channel strategy, pricing, positioning, compliance, and more). jobs.title: Lab Manager IV
jobs.description: Why we're hiringWe run several robotics labs and are standing up more. Today, lab build-out, vendor coordination, safety and change management, and spares are handled in the margins by researchers and engineers, and it slows the research down. We want one person who owns the physical and operational readiness of every robotics lab, so the teams in them can spend their time on robots.What you'll own • Lab build-out and reconfiguration: floor plans, benches, robot cells, power, network, fixturing, safety guarding. Take a space from empty to running, and reconfigure it as programs change. • Change management for the labs: intake requests, assess impact on ongoing experiments, schedule the work, communicate downtime, and keep a record of what changed and when. • Safety and facilities coordination, including DHS and EHS partners: risk assessments, permits and approvals, hazardous material handling, LOTO and machine guarding, incident follow-up, and keeping the labs audit-ready. • Vendors and external partners: scope work, get quotes, manage installs and service visits, hold vendors to schedule and quality, and own the relationship day to day. • Procurement: build and track purchase requests for equipment, tooling, components, and consumables. Work lead times backwards from program dates and flag the ones that put a milestone at risk. • Spares and inventory: define what we hold, where, and at what depth for critical robot components. Set up tracking, run cycle counts, and make sure a failed actuator does not stop a lab for a week. • Asset and equipment lifecycle: tagging, calibration and maintenance schedules, service records, decommissioning and transfers between sites. • Lab operations: access and onboarding for new lab users, documented standard practices, shared tool and station scheduling, and the basic hygiene that keeps a shared space usable. • First-line troubleshooting on the stations. When a rig stops working, you are the first person there: isolate whether it's power, cabling, a controller, a sensor, the network, or software, fix what you can, and hand off a clear diagnosis with what you already ruled out when you can't. • Keeping stations current. Track what firmware, driver, controller, and software versions each station is on, schedule updates in windows that don't interrupt data collection, verify the station still works afterwards, and roll back when it doesn't. • Networking and IT. Own the working relationship with IT and HelpDesk for lab networking, switch ports, VLANs, wired and wireless coverage, static addressing for robots and cameras, and machine imaging or access. Open and drive the tickets yourself instead of routing researchers into the queue. • Station configuration as a known state. Each station has documented cabling, addressing, mounted hardware, and installed versions, so a rig can be rebuilt or reproduced rather than rediscovered. • Uptime and recurring issues. Log downtime and its causes, spot the failures that keep coming back, and fix the root cause with the vendor, IT, or the owning engineer. • Program management on top of all of it: a single view of lab readiness across sites, dependencies and risks surfaced early, and regular status to the research and engineering leads you support.What we're looking for • 8+ years in lab, facility, hardware, or manufacturing operations, with at least a few of those owning a space or program end to end. • Real project or program management experience: schedules, dependencies, budgets, and the judgment to escalate a slipping lead time before it becomes a missed milestone. • Hands-on comfort in a hardware environment. You can read a floor plan, spec power and pneumatics, assemble a station, and talk credibly with a machinist, an electrician, and a controls engineer. • Experience coordinating safety and compliance work with EHS or equivalent partners, including risk assessments and permits for machinery or hazardous materials. • Procurement and vendor management experience: quotes, POs, statements of work, and holding suppliers accountable. • Inventory and spares management, ideally with an actual system of record rather than a spreadsheet you inherited. • Strong written communication. Much of this job is telling a dozen busy people what is changing, when, and what they need to do about it.Nice to have • Robotics, automation, or test-lab experience: robot arms, grippers, end effectors, motion control, sensor rigs. • Enough comfort on the software and network side to be useful: Linux basics, the command line, reading logs, simple scripting, and understanding IP addressing and switching well enough to work a problem with IT rather than just report it. • Familiarity with industrial robot safety standards and machine guarding. • Experience standing up a new site or lab from an empty room. • Basic CAD for layout work, and comfort with inventory, asset, or ticketing tools.How we'll measure success • Labs come online on the dates the programs are planning around. • Researchers are not doing their own purchasing, chasing vendors, or hunting for spares. • Critical spares are on the shelf, and unplanned downtime is short and rare. • Station problems get triaged and resolved without a researcher having to chase IT or a vendor. • Stations are on known, current versions, and updates land without surprising anyone mid-experiment. • Safety and compliance obligations are met without a scramble before an audit. • Leads know the state of every lab without having to ask.The pay range that Tundra in good faith reasonably expects to pay for this position is $43.54/hour - $54.42/hour. jobs.description: Job Title: Design Project ManagerThe Client Project Manager (CPM) serves as the primary liaison between the Client Design Project Lead (DPL) and all key project stakeholders. Operating with significant autonomy on-site, the CPM drives continuous project progression, delivers structured weekly status reports, and escalates matters to the DPL exclusively when proposed actions impact budget, schedule, core design scope, or operational and installation standards. Furthermore, the CPM guarantees full coverage and seamless continuity during any planned absences throughout the engagement term.Core Responsibilities & Scope of Work:1. Owner Representation & Stakeholder ManagementSingle Point of Contact: Serve as the dedicated on-site representative for the Owner, safeguarding corporate interests across all site-level operations and decisions.Requirements & Deliverables: Communicate, monitor, and enforce accountability regarding the Owner's functional requirements and project deliverables.Documentation & Governance: Maintain comprehensive, real-time documentation of key decisions, formal approvals, field progress, and risk logs within designated tracking systems to guarantee complete transparency and auditability.Meeting Governance: Participate in all principal Design and Construction Administration (CA) progress meetings; align continuously with the Client DPL on strategic expectations.Status Reporting: Generate and submit formal weekly project status reports to the Owner Project Lead utilizing prescribed reporting frameworks.Stakeholder Alignment: Manage expectations through clear, timely, and executive communication. Coordinate directly with operational end-users to integrate technical requirements in compliance with established Owner Standards.2. Commercial & Contract ManagementContractual Compliance: Ensure all execution complies strictly with contractual terms, maintaining rigorous accountability across the design team.Consultant Coordination: Act as the primary field contact for third-party consultants (e.g., TEOR PM), ensuring synchronization across schedules, deliverables, and field activities.Change Control: Rigorously evaluate design modifications, omissions, scope variations, and potential change orders, presenting formal recommendations to the Client DPL for final determination.Audit Records: Ensure the Engineer of Record (EOR) maintains precise, timely records of all design instructions, field changes, and administrative determinations.3. Schedule & Execution OversightSchedule Optimization: Proactively track the master design schedule and main construction timeline to detect risks, optimize path sequences, and oversee direct vendor dependencies.Milestone Tracking: Monitor critical path milestones, reporting schedule variances, impact analyses, and proposed mitigation plans to the Client DPL.Issue Resolution: Facilitate immediate resolution of design-related field challenges by orchestrating cross-functional resources and escalating unresolvable risks appropriately.4. Quality Assurance & Quality Control (QA/QC)Quality Monitoring: Collaborate with the Owner QA/QC Lead to evaluate active construction against technical specifications, design intent, and acceptance standards.Reporting Integrity: Validate the detail, accuracy, and risk mitigation strategies in weekly EOR discipline submissions.Design Conformance: Hold design partners accountable for maintaining complete alignment with authorized construction documents throughout execution.Close-Out Management: Oversee close-out activities with direct-appointed vendors, ensuring full regulatory compliance and statutory certification acquisition.Continuous Improvement: Lead post-completion debriefs to document lessons learned and operational enhancements.5. jobs.title: Audio Engineer IV
jobs.description: About the teamReality Labs Research at Meta brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality. One focus of the Reality Labs Research Audio team is redefining human hearing — allowing people to feel together despite being physically apart, and to converse in even the most difficult listening environments.SummaryWe are looking for an experienced contract Acoustic Engineer to own day-to-day acoustic measurement, evaluation, and tuning for a wearable audio program in our Redmond acoustic labs. The role is hands-on and lab-based: build and maintain acoustic test rigs, run daily measurement sweeps against new algorithm and firmware builds, maintain regression tracking so tuning regressions are caught early, and translate measurement results into concrete, actionable tuning recommendations for algorithm and hardware teams. The work also supports speech-enhancement development for smart glasses.Job ResponsibilitiesDesign and execute repeatable acoustic test protocols in anechoic, semi-anechoic, and reverberant rooms, including impulse response and transfer function measurements, reverberation and noise-field characterization, and calibration and traceability of the full measurement chain.Build and calibrate realistic speech-in-noise scenes (babble, diffuse and directional interferers, restaurant / cocktail-party conditions) and SNR-controlled playback setups; score speech-in-noise performance across seating geometries, head orientations, and talker distances.Characterize loudspeakers and transducers: frequency and phase response, sensitivity, distortion (THD/IMD, Rub & Buzz), directivity and polar patterns, max SPL and compression behavior, and leakage/fit sensitivity for wearable form factors.Quantify signal-enhancement behavior — directivity index, noise reduction, speech distortion, target/interferer suppression trade-offs, latency, and artifact/musical-noise characterization — and assess stability across real-world acoustic conditions.Operate and maintain multichannel capture rigs: microphone-array calibration and channel matching, clock/sync and latency management, gain staging, and anti-aliasing.Perform iterative acoustic tuning of gain, EQ, compression, directionality, and enhancement parameters against objective intelligibility and quality metrics (e.g. STI, STOI/ESTOI, HASPI/HASQI, SII, PESQ/POLQA, SNR improvement), and validate settings with listener-facing checks.Characterize the effect of the wireless transport path on enhanced speech — bandwidth limiting, codec artifacts, packet loss and dropout behavior, and end-to-end / conversational-turn latency — in partnership with wireless engineering.Develop Python or MATLAB tooling for automated analysis, batch processing, and regression dashboards.Establish shared test protocols, calibration references, and reporting formats so that results are reproducible and comparable across Meta and external partner labs; support joint test sessions and partner-facing measurement reviews.Triage acoustic issues raised by researchers, cross-functional partners, and external collaborators, and document methods and results in clear technical reports.SkillsStrong understanding of acoustics, electroacoustic measurement, signal flow, and microphone functionality, selection, and placement.Hands-on fluency with acoustic test equipment and software (e.g. Audio Precision APx, Klippel, Brüel & Kjær, SoundCheck) and with HATS/manikins and artificial ears for on-device and on-ear measurement.Working knowledge of speech-enhancement algorithms — multi-microphone beamforming, adaptive noise cancellation, AGC / dynamic range compression, dereverberation, and ML-based enhancement front-ends — and the ability to interpret algorithm behavior from measurement data and give actionable feedback to algorithm developers.Proficiency in Python or MATLAB for measurement automation, analysis, and reporting.Strong experimental discipline: able to define the metric, build the rig, run the sweep, interpret the trade-offs, recommend a setting, and validate it.Ability to work independently in a lab environment and sustain a daily experimental cadence; strong attention to detail and clear technical communication.Minimum RequirementsBS or MS in acoustics, electrical engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.3+ years of hands-on acoustic measurement experience in controlled laboratory settings.Demonstrated experience with audio signal processing and objective audio/speech quality evaluation.On-site in Redmond, WA is required — the work is lab-dependent.Preferred QualificationsPrior work on multi-microphone speech enhancement for wearable devices.Experience with prototype hardware devices and with designing or commissioning acoustic lab spaces.Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality technical reports.Pursuant to the California Fair Chance Act, Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, qualified applicants will be considered for assignment with arrest and conviction records. jobs.title: Research Scientist I
jobs.description: Part-Time Researcher — Mechanism Design for Generative RankingRole summaryMeta's Ads Ranking AI Research team seeks a part-time researcher for a 12-month collaborative project on mechanism design for generative feed ranking — studying how auction mechanisms should be designed when a generative model produces an entire content sequence rather than inserting sponsored items into a fixed ordering. The work spans formal theory and computational experimentation, and is expected to result in publications at top-tier venues.Responsibilities- Derive bounds quantifying the revenue and welfare implications of constrained versus jointly optimized sequence ordering- Characterize incentive compatibility when contextual effects make an item's surrounding context endogenous to bids- Design and analyze monotone mechanisms, including affine maximizer auctions, maximal-in-range mechanisms with learned range generators, and monotonicity-constrained autoregressive architectures- Build simulation environments for synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments, and co-author research publicationsExperience required- Currently enrolled in a PhD program in computer science, economics, operations research, or a related field, with at least 2 years of doctoral research completed. jobs.title: Designer IV
jobs.description: CREATIVE X : GENERATIVE AI ARTIST, PERFORMANCE MARKETINGABOUT OUR TEAMCreative X is a global, integrated creative agency that drives the creative vision for our brands and how they are perceived in the world. We develop the vision for next-generation creative advertising for Meta, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and our hardware products.ABOUT THIS ROLECreative X's performance marketing reaches the businesses that grow on Meta's platforms, and generative AI is how that work gets made now. It is the medium we work in every day, across every project, rather than a capability we are beginning to explore.As our Generative AI Artist, you make the images. An art director brings you the concept and the direction. You originate the visual and image-making approach that realizes it, then generate imagery finished enough to run as advertising. You also own our generative pipeline, including Weavy, building and documenting the workflows the rest of the team produces in.This is a craft role, and the craft is the whole point. What you own is the image: how it gets made, how good it is, and how repeatably we can make the next one. Nobody here will tell you which model to reach for or how to build the graph. That judgment is the reason we are hiring you.RESPONSIBILITIESGenerate market-ready imagery for digital B2B performance/direct response advertising, working from an art director's concept and direction.Originate the visual and image-making approach that realizes the concept, including model selection and chaining, prompt architecture, reference and style systems, iteration and refinement.Own, build, and document our generative pipeline, including Weavy node graphs, prompt systems, reference libraries, and style locks, so other people can run them.Hold image quality, brand systems, and product accuracy in generative output, and know precisely where the model falls short and where a human hand needs to take over.Hand off finished imagery to designers and motion designers in a state they can build production assets from.Evaluate emerging models and tools as they ship, and fold the ones that earn their place into how the team works.MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSGenerative image craftA full portfolio of shipped, client-facing commercial work of the highest caliber, where you personally generated the imagery. jobs.title: Data Labeling Analyst II
jobs.description: Technical Data Labeling Analyst (Automation Specialist)About the RoleWe're looking for automation-minded analysts to join our team as Technical Data Labeling Analysts. This is primarily an automation and tooling role — you'll spend most of your time designing workflows, building AI-assisted processes, and writing SQL to make labeling operations faster and more reliable. The labeling work you do (~20% of the role) keeps you close enough to the content to know what's worth automating.You'll sit within the Product Data Operations (PDO) team, working alongside program managers and partnering with global vendor teams. Where a DLA focuses on labeling quality and program operations, a TDLA builds the tooling and automations that make the whole team more efficient.What You'll DoAutomation and Tooling (~80%)Design and maintain workflow automations (using platforms like n8n) for repetitive operational tasks — data pulls, report generation, quality metric rollupsBuild AI-assisted flows for classification, extraction, and summarization to support labeling quality at scalePull and analyze data using SQL to support quality reporting and root-cause analysisAnalyze existing workflows for inefficiency and propose automation opportunities to program managersWrite concise documentation and playbooks so teammates can self-serve on automations you've builtMonitor, debug, and iterate on deployed automations for reliability and accuracyCollaborate with program managers and product partners to translate operational pain points into tooling solutionsLabeling and Quality (~20%)Practice labeling in assigned queues to stay close to the workflows you're automatingPerform quality assurance on labeled datasets — identifying systematic errors, inconsistencies, and guideline gapsContribute to guideline development by flagging ambiguities and proposing decision boundary refinementsReview edge cases and write clear rationales that explain classification decisionsProgram OperationsPartner with vendor teams and attend business reviews to track quality metrics against targetsEscalate tooling issues and bugs to engineering teams with structured documentationShare knowledge and best practices with peer DLAs and TDLAs across programsYou need to understand the labeling work deeply enough to automate it well — that's why you stay hands-on. But the majority of your impact comes from the tooling and workflows you build for the team.What We're Looking ForRequiredStrong critical reasoning ability — you can hold ambiguity, weigh competing interpretations, and arrive at defensible judgmentsExceptional attention to detail and consistency across high-volume, repetitive tasks without quality degradationClear, precise written communication — not literary polish, but the ability to convey a decision and its rationale without ambiguityComfort applying structured rule sets and decision trees to messy, real-world contentAbility to self-calibrate — recognizing when your own judgment is drifting and correcting courseProactive problem identification — when you see the same error pattern three times, you flag the systemic issue, not just the individual instancesAbility to look at a manual process and see the automation opportunity — you instinctively ask "can this be a workflow?"Comfort translating a business need into a structured automation design, even without writing code from scratchReliable, self-directed work ethic suited to a contractor environment with distributed collaborationPreferred backgrounds (any of the following are strong signals)Operations or business analyst — experience identifying process inefficiencies and building automated solutions, even if informalData analyst — comfort with SQL, spreadsheet-based data pipelines, and turning raw data into actionable reportingQA or test engineer — experience with systematic process validation, test automation, or quality frameworksTechnical program support — experience bridging business teams and engineering, translating requirements into tooling solutionsWe also value experience in content moderation or trust & safety, clinical research coordination, and data annotation or labeling roles.TechnicalSQL for data exploration and reporting — you can write queries to pull metrics, investigate quality issues, and support analysisExperience with or strong interest in low-code/no-code automation platforms (n8n, Make, Zapier, or similar)Comfort with data structures, basic scripting logic, and connecting systems through built-in integrationsAbility to read and interpret quality metrics (agreement rates, confusion matrices, accuracy scores)Familiarity with or willingness to learn annotation toolingAI tool fluency — willingness to experiment with AI for analysis, drafting, and workflow automationWhat Makes Someone SucceedThe people who excel in this role share a few traits that go beyond the resume:They automate the second time. The first time they do a task manually to understand it. The second time, they build a workflow so nobody has to do it manually again.They write for constraint, not beauty. They can draft a decision rule that eliminates ambiguity — closer to legal specification than creative writing.They think in systems, not just instances. When reviewing a batch of labels, they notice the pattern behind individual errors and trace it back to a guideline gap or training deficit.They're comfortable being wrong and recalibrating. Labeling work requires updating your internal model as guidelines evolve — rigid thinkers struggle here.They care about why, not just what. They don't just classify something correctly — they can explain the reasoning in a way that helps others do the same.They collaborate across distance and time zones. They communicate clearly in writing, close the loop without being chased, and build trust with partners they may never meet in person.This posting is for a contract assignment with Tundra Technical Solutions to provide services to Meta. jobs.description: Human Interface Pitch Human Interface Design (HI) is the product design organization within Meta's Reality Labs. We are designing the experiences that will define the next era of computing across the full spectrum of Meta’s hardware and spatial computing platforms. Our ambition is to make intelligence feel natural, empowering, and deeply human. It's a rare moment to define a new category, and design is central to winning it. The team operates as a studio. This means designers have the opportunity to move between projects and product areas, giving individuals a breadth of experience across some of the most ambitious and technically complex design challenges in the industry. We're an in-person design culture, collaborating 3+ days per week at our Design hubs. Rapid prototyping, hands-on hardware access, and real-time feedback on physical products require us to be in the same space, working shoulder-to-shoulder in these locations:Mobile (Rachel Diamond)Horizon Consumer CoreThe Horizon Consumer Core design team is responsible for the player-facing experience — where people discover, play, and remix games they love with friends. We're designing the end-to-end journey of how people find games that match their interests, connect with friends through shared play, use agents to make the games their own, and participate in a digital economy. The design challenges span cross-platform interaction models, social systems at scale, discovery and engagement loops, and building trust in emerging paradigms. Social gaming is the future, and we are poised to make a big splash in the market later this year. Horizon Creator ToolsThe Horizon Creator Tools design team is responsible for Meta's suite of AI-native creation tools that empowers anyone to build rich 2D and 3D games — no coding or modeling expertise required. We're designing across desktop and mobile to enable creators to bring their ideas to life wherever they are, in minutes and without a large studio budget. jobs.title: Systems Engineer II
jobs.description: Summary: The main function of a systems engineer is to apply the principles of computer science and mathematical analysis to the design, development, testing, and evaluation of the software and systems that make computers work. A typical systems engineer analyzes user needs, and then designs, tests, and develops software to meet those needs. jobs.description: The Electronics Verification Engineer is responsible for validating and qualifying electronic hardware from prototype through production. On a day-to-day basis, this role involves hands-on board bring-up and bench testing using lab instrumentation (oscilloscopes, DMMs, power supplies, etc.), executing validation plans against design requirements, troubleshooting circuit-level failures, performing PCB rework, and capturing/analyzing test data. The engineer writes and maintains test procedures, documents results in clear lab reports, tracks issues to resolution with cross-functional teams, and supports NPI milestones (EVT/DVT/PVT). jobs.title: Clinical Trial Contract Manager
jobs.description: The Clinical Trial Contract Manager is responsible for assurance that clinical trial /site budget is of high quality and allocations are within fair market values. This role is responsible for the development and maintenance of Sites Fee Framework as well as timely and accurate coordination, processing, monitoring, and administration of payments to sites according to budget and terms. The incumbent will be responsible for the support of management goals and objectives of the department. As an employee of Boehringer Ingelheim, you will actively contribute to the discovery, development, and delivery of our products to our patients and customers. Our global presence provides opportunity for all employees to collaborate internationally, offering visibility and opportunity to directly contribute to the companies' success. We realize that our strength and competitive advantage lie with our people. We support our employees in several ways to foster a healthy working environment, meaningful work, mobility, networking, and work-life balance. jobs.title: Engineering Support Specialist
jobs.description: Location: Tarzana, CADuration: 12 months w/possibility of extension Pay: $51 per hour Position SummaryThe Metrology Engineer is responsible for the administration and coordination of both Tarzana and Santa Monica instrument and equipment calibration. At AstraZeneca, Maintenance Planner & Scheduler is responsible for planning, coordinating, and scheduling preventive, predictive, corrective, and shutdown maintenance and calibration activities for manufacturing, laboratory, utility, and facility systems that support cell therapy operations. This role requires strong technical understanding of GMP-regulated environments, critical utilities, cleanroom operations, and process equipment used in advanced therapy manufacturing.The role ensures maintenance & calibration works are executed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with quality, regulatory, and site reliability requirements. support uninterrupted clinical and commercial supply Key Responsibilities:• Metrology/Calibration Planning: Develop detailed work plans for preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, predictive maintenance, calibration coordination, and reliability-based tasks for manufacturing, supply chain, lab and facility assets.• Calibration Scheduling: Create and maintain daily, weekly, and longer-range maintenance schedules, balancing production priorities, equipment availability, labor capacity, and shutdown windows.• CMMS Management: Manage work orders in the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), ensuring accurate asset hierarchies, task lists, labor estimates, spare parts, and maintenance history.• Job Plan Development: Build standardized job plans with clear scope, required tools, materials, permits, lockout/tagout needs, craft labor, vendor support, and estimated durations.• Coordination with Operations: Work closely with manufacturing, facilities, and lab stakeholders to align maintenance windows with production campaigns, aseptic processing constraints, and cleanroom access requirements.• Technical Equipment Support: Plan maintenance activities for process and facility equipment such as HVAC systems, HEPA filtration units, air handling units, clean steam systems, RO water systems, compressed gases, freezers, incubators, biosafety cabinets, isolators, autoclaves, pass-through chambers, centrifuges, LN2 systems, refrigeration systems, pumps, valves, sensors, PLC-controlled skids, and building management systems.• GMP Compliance: Ensure maintenance activities are planned and documented in accordance with GMP, GDP, site procedures, change control, deviation management, and data integrity requirements.• Shutdown and Turnaround Planning: Support site shutdowns, planned outages, and major maintenance events by developing integrated schedules, sequencing tasks, and coordinating internal and external resources.• Spare Parts and Materials Coordination: Identify required spare parts, consumables, and contractor services in advance of scheduled work; partner with warehouse, procurement, and engineering to avoid delays.• Risk-Based Prioritization: Prioritize maintenance tasks based on safety, product impact, compliance risk, equipment criticality, and operational urgency.• KPI Tracking: Monitor and report maintenance metrics such as schedule compliance, Calibration and PM completion/compliance, backlog health, mean time between failure (MTBF), mean time to repair (MTTR), % utilization and downtime trends.• Contractor/Vendor Coordination: Coordinate service providers and OEM technicians for specialized maintenance, ensuring proper site access, permits, training, and documentation.• Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to improve maintenance effectiveness, planning accuracy, spare parts strategy, and equipment reliability through RCM, FMEA-informed maintenance, and lessons learned. Technical Scope / Equipment KnowledgeThe role should demonstrate working knowledge of maintenance planning and scheduling for equipment commonly found in cell therapy manufacturing facilities, including:• Cleanroom infrastructure: HVAC, differential pressure control, temperature/humidity monitoring, HEPA systems, airlocks, environmental monitoring support systems, and building automation controls.• Critical utilities: RO water, clean steam, chilled water, process gases, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, and electrical distribution systems.• Process equipment: Biosafety cabinets, incubators, centrifuges, controlled-rate freezers, cryogenic storage systems, water baths, microscopes, and single-use support equipment.• Cold chain and cryogenic systems: -80 freezers, LN2 freezers, cryo storage vessels, monitoring/alarm systems, and backup systems supporting chain of identity and chain of custody requirements.• Instrumentation and controls: Sensors, transmitters, alarms, PLCs, SCADA/BMS/EMS interfaces, calibration interfaces, and automated skid packages.• Facility systems: Fire protection, emergency power, UPS, generators, security-controlled access interfaces, and waste handling systems relevant to classified GMP spaces. Required Qualifications• Associate's, vocational, certificate, technical, or equivalent bachelor’s degree/diploma with equivalent experience in the related technical discipline, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.• Experience in metrology and maintenance planning and scheduling within biopharmaceutical, cell therapy, gene therapy, vaccine, pharmaceutical, medical device, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.• Strong technical understanding of facility systems, utilities, and process equipment maintenance.• Minimum 3 years of relevant work experience in maintenance group within a regulated environment w/college degree.• 5-7 years of experience with HS diploma• Experience using CMMS such as SAP PM / Beamex CMX, Maximo, BMRAM or equivalent.• Knowledge of GMP, EHS, lockout/tagout, permit-to-work systems, deviation/change control awareness, and maintenance documentation practices.• Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, equipment manuals, engineering drawings, one-line diagrams, and maintenance procedures.• Strong coordination, organizational, and cross-functional communication skills.• Familiarity with reliability-centered maintenance, predictive maintenance tools, and asset criticality assessments.• Understanding of calibration coordination, commissioning/qualification interfaces, and validated systems in GMP environments.• Certification or training in maintenance planning, project scheduling, or reliability methods is an advantage.

jobs.description: Location: Tarzana, CADuration: 6 months (possible chance of FTE conversion)Shift: 1stWorking Hours: Monday-Friday (6:30am-3:30pm)Pay: $45-48 Position Summary:The Senior Maintenance HVAC Technician is responsible for ensuring reliable, compliant, and efficient operation of HVAC and environmental control systems for GMP facilities in Tarzana, CA. This role leads complex maintenance and troubleshooting activities for cleanrooms, laboratories, and production areas; manages critical utilities that impact product quality; and drives continuous improvement initiatives aligned with regulatory standards such as FDA, & EU GMP Standards. The technician serves as a subject matter expert for HVAC, Building Management Systems (BMS)/SCADA, Cleanroom Pressurization, Temperature/Humidity Control, HEPA Filtration, and Environmental Monitoring, mentoring junior technicians and collaborating closely with Quality, Engineering, EHS, and Operations. Overall, the role focuses on maintaining all HVAC System to control temperature, humidity, differential pressure, and air quality to protect product quality, personnel safety, and regulatory compliance. Essential Functions and Responsibilities• HVAC Operations & Reliability: Perform preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance on air handlers, chillers, boilers, heat exchangers, VAVs, exhaust systems, dehumidifiers, and split systems to maintain controlled temperature, humidity, airflow, and pressurization in GMP spaces.• Cleanroom & GMP Compliance: Maintain environmental conditions per ISO 14644 classifications and facility SOPs; ensure proper HEPA filter integrity, airflow patterns, recovery times, and differential pressures; support gowning airlocks and aseptic areas.• BMS/EMS/SCADA Management: Monitor, tune, and troubleshoot Building Management Systems and Environmental Monitoring Systems; implement setpoint strategies, alarm rationalization, and sequence-of-operations adjustments; document changes per change-control.• Calibration & Qualification Support: Coordinate and perform periodic calibration of sensors (temperature, RH, pressure, flow) and support HVAC system IQ/OQ/PQ activities; generate and review qualification protocols and reports.• Troubleshooting & Root Cause Analysis: Lead investigations of deviations, alarms, and environmental excursions; apply RCA methods (5-Why, Fishbone) and implement robust corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).• Documentation & GMP Records: Complete accurate work orders, maintenance logs, and calibration records; author and revise SOPs, job plans, and standard work; maintain asset history compliant with cGMP and GDP requirements.• Regulatory & Audit Readiness: Support internal and external audits (e.g., FDA, Internal); provide evidence of maintenance, calibration, and qualification; ensure systems remain in validated state and changes follow formal Change Control.• Energy & Performance Optimization: Analyze HVAC performance, energy consumption, and lifecycle costs; jobs.description: Cleanroom Inspection and Packaging TechnicianDutiesKeysight’s Semiconductor Infrastructure Solutions Division is seeking a Cleanroom Inspection and Packaging Technician. jobs.title: Clinical Study Supply Lead
jobs.description: Location: Gaithersburg, MDHybrid Schedule (3 days onsite, 2 days remote)Duration: 12 monthsPay: $55 per hour AstraZeneca is a major international healthcare business engaged in the research, development, manufacture and marketing of prescription pharmaceuticals and the supply of healthcare services. AstraZeneca is proud to offer a unique workplace culture that inspires innovation and collaboration. Co-workers are empowered to express diverse perspectives - and are made to feel valued, energized and rewarded for their ideas and creativity. Would you like to utilize your planning and supply chain knowledge to lead clinical supplies for your portfolio of global clinical studies? With constant new products and launches, there has never been a better time to join Global Clinical Supply Chain and shape our future with a significant contribution to life-changing medicines. We have an exciting opportunity for talented Clinical Study Supply Lead to join our Clinical Study Supply Chain team in Gaithersburg, Maryland. This is a key role within our Clinical Manufacturing and Supply teams, and we make sure clinical trial medications are available at the right quality, in the right quantity at the right time for every patient taking part in AstraZeneca’s trials all over the world. Our goal is to never miss a patient. In Pharmaceutical Technology and Development (PT&D) we are the bridge which turns forward-thinking science into actual medicines that help millions of people around the world. We work across the entire value chain, crafting and delivering active ingredients, formulations and devices required to support new medicines – from supplies for use in early toxicology studies and clinical trials to developing the technology to ensure drugs can be scaled up for commercial manufacture. Tasks and responsibilities/The role: In this role you will project manage the design, plan, and set-up of the study supply chain to ensure on time delivery of clinical supplies. You will also lead a cross-functional team enabling continuous dialogue with both internal and external partners on study design requirements and associated changes which may impact the supply chain elements of the study. To be successful in this role you need to be a fast learner, self-driven and comfortable working in a high pace R&D environment. You need to be a collaborative team player, flexible and have strong communication, planning and problem-solving skills. Your main responsibilities will include: • Project manage the delivery of clinical supplies effectively and consistently, and input to the balance of costs and any risks to supply. • Ensure effective communication with project teams and key partners across a global network. • Support risk management of individual studies with proactive mitigation of risks that potentially impact the quality or delivery of supplies. • Take ownership for Inventory management including any rework and recalls, extensions of shelf life and expiry date management, or stock destruction. • Manage the Interactive Response Technology (IRT) system to execute demand and supply planning. • Work within GMP Quality Management Systems ensuring that you actively handle any deviations, complaints and change controls. Essential requirements: • Bachelor’s Degree in a scientific or supply chain subject area – equivalent experience will be considered. • 2-5 years of experience • Some exposure with clinical trials• Experience within a supply chain management environment with a holistic knowledge of end-to-end supply chain activities • Experience of demand planning and forecasting and risk identification and management • Experience in running projects and inﬂuencing customer demands. • Excellent English written and verbal communication skills. • Proficient IT skills with an ability to adapt and operate in bespoke multiple systems. Desirables: • Awareness of GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) and GCP (Good Clinical Practice) • Knowledge of clinical development processes relevant to the supply of clinical materials • Lean knowledge and understanding • Experienced in handling Quality Events (Deviations, Change Controls, Complaints) Soft skills: • Strong inﬂuencing, negotiating and problem-solving skills, across geographical and cultural boundaries • Ability to adapt and operate in bespoke multiple systems. AstraZeneca is one of the world’s most exciting bio-pharmaceutical companies. From scientists to sales, lab techs to legal, we’re on a mission to turn ideas into life-changing medicines that improve patients’ lives and benefit society. We need great people who share our passion for science and have the drive and determination to meet the unmet needs of patients around the world.
